narrative: In the FY2027 base case PBT is about £97M and CET1 stays above 12.3%. A −100 bp Bank Rate path costs about £12M of NII before deposits catch up. The recession case — house prices −15%, unemployment +2 points — lifts ECL to about £38M (75 bps), halves PBT to about £50M and takes CET1 to 11.4%: above the 9.57% requirement, inside the management buffer. A deposit price war is the costliest NII risk (−£15M).
